question: If \(p,\) \(q,\) and \(r\) are distinct roots of \(x^3-x^2+x-2=0,\) then \(p^3+q^3+r^3\) equals
solution:
We can find the symmetric sum without finding the individual roots. Because \(p,q,r\) are the three distinct roots of the monic cubic,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x-p)(x-q)(x-r)
&=x^3-(p+q+r)x^2\\
&\quad +(pq+pr+qr)x-pqr.
\end{aligned}
\]
The coefficient of \(x^2\) comes from selecting one of \(-p,-q,-r\) and two copies of \(x\); the coefficient of \(x\) comes from selecting two of those constants. Comparing with the given polynomial therefore gives
\[
p+q+r=1,
\qquad pq+pr+qr=1.
\]
Consequently,
\[
p^2+q^2+r^2=(p+q+r)^2-2(pq+pr+qr)=-1.
\]
These algebraic identities also hold for nonreal roots.

Every root \(t\) satisfies \(t^3=t^2-t+2\). Applying this to all three roots and adding gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
p^3+q^3+r^3
&=(p^2+q^2+r^2)-(p+q+r)+6\\
&=-1-1+6=4.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(4\) is absent from choices A through D, the answer is \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
